correctness.rationale: With inner product linear in first variable, y=conjugate(q)x+sqrt(1-r²)z for r<1, z perpendicular to x. For fixed x and f=|<Ax,x>|, dim x-perp>=2 makes <Ax,z> fill the full disk of radius sqrt(1-f²). Thus the fiber max is F_r(f)=rf+sqrt(1-r²)sqrt(1-f²). A complex quadratic isotropic-vector argument yields f=0, and path-connectedness of unit sphere gives all 0<=f<s (including s if attained). Scalar Cauchy-Schwarz yields plateau at f=r for r<s and endpoint f=s otherwise, with exact boundary-attainment condition. Unitary scalar rotation of test pair makes the range circular, connected Stiefel domain plus a zero witness makes it a full disk; r=1 handled as sphere case. Infinite block antiunitaries with s_n increasing to nonattained s_infty exhibit genuinely open boundary. Independent 25 scalar-envelope comparisons confirm optimization but do not replace Hilbert geometry.
